title: 'Ebobaleeba' and 'Million Dollar Secret': hits and credit disputes
summary: Humes and Dance sort out the late-1940s hits. 'Ebobaleeba' was her only royalty; 'Million Dollar Secret' for Modern was recorded at the Shrine, and the recording man put his name on it until Mr. Koenig got it removed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Shrine. But it was "Million Dollar Secret".

So 1950. Well, that one that was in 1945, "Ebobaleeba", you know, that was Alladin (records). No, that wasn't "The Shrine", that's right. Well, that "Million Dollar Secret" that comes a little after. We won't get to that quite so quickly. Now let me see.
Big money making hits that you had on records. I mean, "Ebobaleeba" was a big hit.
And you did get some royalties from that, didn't you?
Yeah, that was the only royalty I ever got.
Well, when you made the "Million Dollar Secret" for the Modern (Records) people, that was Shrine auditorium, wasn't it?
Yes, it was at the Shrine. I made it at the session too.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Oh, at the same time too?
Oh, I don't know about the same time.
I don't remember that. But I know I made it, and the man who recorded it, he put his name on it. It was supposed to be his number. And then Mr. Koenig had a terrible time getting his name off of it.
Well, that's the way they all do it. You know, you have something and they go and say they did it and you ain't paying no attention.
Yes, that's right. You didn't really get the royalties off that?
